title: Compute-path adjudicator with seqlen forecasting and quantized warmstarts
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We observe elevated tail latency for mixed workloads where short-prefill but long-decode requests are sent to kernels optimized for prefill throughput, and quantized fallback choices are selected without warm-start costs considered. Goal: Implement a compute-path adjudicator that uses per-request seqlen forecasting + model quantization warmstart estimates to pick an execution path (kernel variant, layout, and quant level) minimizing expected p95/p99 latency subject to cost constraints.

Scope: runtime decision only (no model training). This ticket covers heuristic design, lightweight forecasting model, warmstart cost estimator, runtime integration API, canary rollout and observability dashboards. Follow-on tickets will handle long-term RL/autotune and cross-customer policy management.

Non-goals: full offline autotuner, multi-model global optimizer, scheduler-level GPU preemption changes.

Key constraints and assumptions: 1) Forecasts must be sub-ms to compute per-request. 2) Warmstart penalty for quantized kernels is dominated by KV/cache reprovisioning and memory layout migration; we will approximate from microbenchmarks. 3) Must interoperate with existing route fallback policies and canary feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: Adjudicator produces a deterministic path decision (variant, quant_level, layout_hint) within 0.8ms median decision time in p95 environment
End-to-end p95 latency improves by >=8% and p99 by >=5% on mixed short-prefill/long-decode synthetic workload compared to baseline routing
No regression (>2%) in peak throughput for throughput-sensitive benchmarks
Telemetry emitted: decision_reason, forecast_seqlen, warmstart_penalty_us, chosen_variant, fallback_reason
Canary rollout mechanism implemented with per-customer opt-in and automatic rollback on latency/regression signals
decision_history: 2025-02-14: Chosen 'adjudicator' naming to emphasize policy arbitration between compute paths rather than a single tuner component
2025-02-18: Decided to implement lightweight seqlen forecaster (linear-prob model + histogram features) instead of heavy LSTM to keep decision cost low
2025-02-22: Warmstart cost will be estimated from microbenchmarks per-arch/quant pair and stored in a small lookup table averaged by model family
2025-02-26: Integrate with existing route polices—adjudicator provides a score and 'do_not_override' flag for high-priority SLA routes
steps: Design and document adjudicator API and decision payload (see links)
Implement seqlen forecaster service module with model-family heuristics and per-request fast features
Build warmstart cost estimator and offline microbenchmark harness to populate the lookup table
Implement adjudicator scoring function combining forecast, warmstart_penalty, kernel_latency_estimates and cost weights
Add telemetry and traces for decision path; wire into Console dashboards for per-route analysis
Create canary rollout with per-customer feature flag and automated SLO checks
Run synthetic benchmarks, followed by internal beta and staged customer canaries
